text:
ConocoPhillips dropped 1.1% today to $134.28, falling back after a sharp three-day rally that peaked at $137.20 on September 2nd. The decline comes as oil prices have pulled back slightly—U.S. crude is at $91.48 per barrel after a volatile week of geopolitical escalation between Iran and the U.S. that had pushed prices higher earlier this week. The stock has now given up most of those gains, suggesting investors are taking profits or reassessing the durability of the energy price surge.

The broader context is mixed for energy stocks. While refinery disruptions in Russia and Ukraine are keeping diesel prices at record highs—which can boost refiner and integrated producer margins—the Iran-U.S. conflict appears to have de-escalated enough to ease immediate oil-price panic. At the same time, new geopolitical risks from the Falklands dispute and Iran's growing isolation under EU sanctions add longer-term unpredictability to global energy flows and could constrain future demand growth.
